items.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Benny Golson took you to San Francisco for a three-week stand at the Jazz Workshop with Curtis Fuller... this turned into your first important engagement because in 1959, this lead to the Jazztet.

ctx.x: Really? I haven’t seen Curtis in a while. So he’s living here? That’s good, I might give him a call one day. Kimery: I have his number.
Yeah I appreciate that, just to say hi. We go way back, that would be nice. I think I saw him once since he has been in town, but it’s been a while so I’d like to.

items.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We brought McCoy Tyner into New York and got him an apartment... We were to do nothing but rehearse... The group was awfully successful

ctx.x: Art came in as the other group. They always hire two groups at The Five Spot. First, it was Randy Weston and his quartet. So, Art came in with Jerry Mulligan. The first (inaudible), Benny said, "Curtis, going to try and put a group together. You write good for sextet. Why don't we get this group? I talked to Donald Byrd about it and he wants to do it." Donald really didn't want to do it. I knew Donald he was going for a bigger shot with The Blackbirds. But, he was bending his first choice. It got to be and we had…
So it was originally a cooperative group?
